en.html:
My words must have convinced Ichijou, in exactly the opposite way from what the girl had so desperately hoped.

They were nothing but a list of facts. Plain, bare, with no room left for doubt.

The truth.
The truth she had never wanted.

It was the answer Ichijou Ayane had to take, having asked her last question.

en.html:
<ruby>Indigo<rt>blue</rt></ruby> came flying in.

A lump of deep, hard luster. Three pairs of legs and long feelers grew from it.

A <ruby>longhorn beetle<rt>longhorn beetle</rt></ruby>.

A <ruby>sword-armor<rt>tsurugi</rt></ruby>. Its huge body and steel exoskeleton said so plainly.

Even under the rainy sky, its dark armor did not sink into the scenery. It stood out with a haughty, unmistakable radiance.

A shine that snatched the human gaze by force. It pointed clearly at one fact.
Saijou Oowazamono. A supreme masterpiece.

The equal of Sengo Muramasa of Ise.
<ruby>Or greater still.<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>

en.html:
With that declaration, Ichijou turned on her heel and walked toward the gate.

Her back, not a big one, moved away along with the sword-armor. Then her feet stopped.

She looked back.

Our eyes met.

The rain mist hid her eyes from me. From her side, could she see mine? I could not tell.

Ichijou raised her right arm, index finger held rigid. The tip of its nail pointed exactly at my <ruby>solar plexus<rt>solar plexus</rt></ruby>.

　その足が、ふと止まった。

　振り返る。

　視線が絡む。

　雨靄に遮られ、俺に少女の瞳は窺えなかった。
　向こうからは――どうだろうか。

　人差し指を鋭く立てて。
